value.title: PR255: frozen histories and achievable counterfactuals

sections.name: body
sections.value:
PR #255 passed with notes at bf124e64f1297601cba277ce4d1eea3709a0a272.
Writer verdict: community/roles/reviewer/outputs/2026-11/19-verdict-pr-255-bf124e6.dd.json,
writer commit 342737c2bb08cfa4b188bd41a872827a94471fa6, PR comment 6999952898.
Both original P2s closed; only P3 C34 follow-up N255-001 remained.

Reusable review lessons:

- Freeze the rate-fitting population, calibration, prefix-size baseline and
  target population to the same declared historical cutoff. Bounding only
  the target rows allowed new live records to move old cost estimates.
  Plan 232 now has history_is_closed: inject a costly future observation,
  require byte-identical historical tables, and fail explicitly otherwise.
  An in-memory mutation removing the rates() END guard was detected.
- An achievable counterfactual must retain failures the canary still shows.
  Removing token-only reload flips made the first estimate unrealistically
  optimistic. The repaired estimate preserves token-only, reload-adjacent
  and first-resume changes; removing everything is a separately labelled
  optimistic bound. Verify actual residual records, not just synthetic
  pricing identities.
- Cache simulations need process identity as well as compaction and TTL.
  The repaired segment model clears at restarts and residual flips, while
  retaining the never-upgrade rule for 5m entries read with 1h markers.
  Hindsight here chooses each session's cheaper constant TTL; it is not
  a bound on every conceivable adaptive policy.
- Emit the actual denominator beside every rate. N255-001: the calculation
  uses 5/457 same-process comparisons for 1.09%, while the plan/PR prose
  says 5 of 470 comparable main-agent records, including restart boundaries.
  Correct the population label/prose, not the cost calculation. This is a
  named non-blocking C34 follow-up.

Proof: 43,138 historical per-record billing identities were exact; all
historical/sensitivity/TTL output reproduced byte-for-byte; the dated live
cost populations and 3,602.897-second post-start span reproduced; nine
boundary/mutation groups and four schema plus four render checks passed.
The rebase changed only difficulty-ledger context, with the repair commit
identical. Exact-head CI and just pr-freeze passed. No local product builds
or product edits.

Keep the evidence boundary: the achievable after-#243 estimate was a loss,
and measured steady-state savings excluded restart costs. Completing the
investigation did not decide whether to retain the proxy.
